newsitem.title: INDIA: India government wins crucial vote in parliament.
newsitem.headline: India government wins crucial vote in parliament.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda won a crucial vote in parliament on Tuesday when his reluctant Congress party ally backed the government's policies spelled out by President Shankar Dayal Sharma last month.

The "motion of thanks to the president's address", which amounts to a vote of confidence, was decided with a voice vote in the lower house of parliament, signalling the first major victory for Deve Gowda in the ongoing budget session.

The rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), India's main opposition group, opposed the motion after several deputies accused the government of involvement in unspecified financial scandals.

"If in nine months, we have been involved in any scam, let them bring a no-cofidence motion against me," Deve Gowda said in his reply to the debate which began after Sharma inaugurated the budget session of parliament on February 20.
"If I am responsible, I will tender my resignation immediately. If any of my ministers is involved I will remove him immediately. Please don't spare us," Deve Gowda said.
His United Front alliance controls fewer than 200 seats in the 545-member Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament, but it has the support of the Congress party's 140 deputies.

Politicians said the government still had to watch out for potential hazards during discussion on the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March), unveiled on February 28 by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. Chidambaram's bold budget cut taxes sharply, held the fiscal deficit for 1996/97 at 5.0 percent and nudged industry towards growth on a path of reforms charted by the preceding Congress government.

Congress leaders hailed the budget as a balanced mix of pro-poor measures and business-friendly policies, putting to rest the question whether Deve Gowda would get the party's crucial support to survive the budget vote.
The BJP, the single largest group in parliament, last month backed off from its proposal to move a no-confidence motion against the nine-month old government.
BJP leaders say they could still move the motion during the budget session which ends on May 12.
